newsitem.title: POLAND: Skinhead held for attack on graves near Auschwitz.
newsitem.headline: Skinhead held for attack on graves near Auschwitz.

text.p: Police have detained a 17-year-old skinhead who admits he vandalised Jewish graves in the southern Polish town adjoining the former Auschwitz death camp, a police spokeswoman said on Friday.
The damage to 43 marble and granite tombstones, toppled or smashed in Oswiecim's pre-World War Two Jewish cemetery, was discovered by a caretaker earlier this week.

Police have accused the technical school pupil under a criminal code article dealing with profanation, which carries a possible jail term of up to three years, spokeswoman Barbara Kucurek told PAP news agency.
She said the skinhead, identified under Polish legal custom only by his first name Tomasz, said he had acted alone.
But this was unlikely given the extent of the damage, added Kocurek, who is based at police headquarters in the provincial capital Bielsko-Biala.

The cemetery is in the centre of Oswiecim and is several kilometres (miles) away from the site of the Auschwitz camp, where World War Two Nazi German occupiers murdered up to 1.5 million people, mostly Jews.
